turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in. Sit. Why are you here?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): For a check-up only. I am really tired, and that wait was endless.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chest pain, yes or no?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't have any chest pain.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you short of breath?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then why have you come today?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): My wife pushed me. I have had high BP for years. Also, climbing the stairs to the flat, something happens, but it is not pain.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): What happens, exactly?

[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, a tight feeling, like squeezing, in the centre of the chest. Climbing stairs brings it, walking fast also, and stairs are worse. If I slow down or I stop, it fades in a minute or two. Well, actually, I would not call it pain.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Only on exertion, not while sitting?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Not while sitting. Only when I push myself. I am tired of saying it.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Since when?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Since Diwali or after. I cannot date it properly. Maybe it started before that also, I really don't know.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any sweating when it comes?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No sweating.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it spread to the arm or the jaw?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It stays in the chest only. And honestly I am fed up. Half an hour for parking, what a waste.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which blood pressure tablet do you take?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlong. For the high BP.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dose, and how many times a day?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Ten mg... no, sorry, five mg. One tablet every morning, by mouth.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): When was Amlong started?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Last winter, or the one before. Don't ask me which, I cannot remember.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any other tablet?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Ecosprin. Aspirin, the small white one.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): What strength, and is it every day?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Seventy-five mg. They told me once a day, but I take it on and off only, whenever I remember.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): You miss doses, then.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. Many days I skip it. I am tired, don't lecture.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. I have never smoked.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your blood pressure is one fifty-two over ninety-four. Pulse is seventy-six.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): It is always like this only. High, yes, I know.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes, it is still high. Chest is clear, no wheeze. Heart sounds are normal, no murmur.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): So am I in trouble or not? Tell me straight, I want to go home.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): This tightness with stairs and fast walking may be angina. I cannot confirm it now.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Angina. I came for a simple check-up and now this.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am ordering an ECG today, and blood tests: fasting sugar, cholesterol, and kidney function.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I have not eaten anything since morning, if that is useful. No extra tests, please, I am done.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fasting is what we want for the sugar and the cholesterol. Take the Ecosprin every day, no skipping. If the tightness starts, stop and rest.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Every day, and rest. I heard. Then what.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it does not settle, or you get sweating or pain in the arm, go to emergency. And see me next week with the reports.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Emergency, next week. Too much. Fine.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Reception will guide you for the ECG and the blood draw before you leave.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, okay. I am going, I need to sit in the car and close my eyes.

spec.situation: Man or woman 50-70 who comes 'for a check-up' and only slowly admits a tight feeling in the chest when climbing stairs or walking fast; first denies chest pain, later describes the tightness. Takes a BP tablet and aspirin on and off. Doctor orders ECG and bloods.
features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

bad.reason: Ecosprin 75 mg is supported, but transcript says taken on and off, not daily.
